one_line_contribution: A zero-rollout statistic — mean pairwise Jaccard overlap of top-k retrieval sets — is offered as a pre-deployment predictor of whether per-instance retrieval over a procedural memory bank can be replaced, verbatim and token-matched, by a fixed subset of that same bank, plus a redundancy (rather than interference) reinterpretation of ReasoningBank's 49.7%@k=1 → 44.4%@k=4 ablation that is decided by an MMR-diversified retrieval cell.
closest_prior_work: Two threats, and the proposal only engages one. (1) arXiv:2511.21730 (Nov 2025), which the author concedes: it establishes on ALFWorld that embedding retrievers over procedural items behave as unordered bags of words and fail to discriminate context — i.e. it already supplies the mediator this proposal proposes to measure, and 2602.02751 plus 2606.23127 already supply the end-to-end direction (saturation, retrieval collapsing the gain). What survives is the overlap law itself, and the law is the part most compromised by the definitional objection below. (2) The threat the Collision Check never looked for at all: the in-context-learning demonstration-selection literature, where per-instance kNN/similarity retrieval of demonstrations versus a single fixed demonstration set has been compared repeatedly and frequently ties, with the tie explained by exactly the mechanism proposed here (near-identical retrieved sets across queries). The frozen-subset swap is that experiment with 'demonstrations' renamed 'procedural memory items'. The proposal distinguishes itself from factual RAG-vs-long-context (Related Work §7) but never from retrieval-vs-fixed demonstration selection, which is far closer to its actual design: same k, same items, verbatim, token-matched, no compiler. A reviewer who knows that line will read A_fix as a known-null ablation transplanted to a new bank type.
strongest_objection: Falsifiable Prediction 1 and the high-overlap half of Prediction 2 are near-tautological, and the design pins both ends of the regression by construction. A_fix is the k highest-dev-frequency items; O is the mean pairwise Jaccard of the top-k sets those items are drawn from. At O = 1.0, A_ret and A_fix are literally the same k items for every instance, so R_fix = 0 by identity, not by measurement — the E2-narrow cell (claimed O > 0.7) and the highest-overlap E1 cells are therefore testing arithmetic plus decoding noise. At O = 0.5 with k=7, roughly half of each query's retrieved items are already in any other query's set, and the frequency-selected fixed subset captures most of the rest, so 'R_fix < 2 points' is what the statistic mechanically implies, not a risky prediction about whether query conditioning carries information. At the other end, both low-overlap anchors are engineered to make R_fix large: B-dup seeds paraphrase near-duplicates of specific test instances (instance-specific by construction, as the proposal says), and E-mix unions two procedurally disjoint families so that a single fixed block must serve both. The leave-one-cell-out test in Prediction 2 then fits a curve whose endpoints are fixed analytically and by design, over ~20 cells that are not independent (shared agent, scaffold, training split, and in most cases the same B_expel bank), with k* — one of the four overlap knobs — chosen per cell to maximize A_ret accuracy, which entangles the predictor with the outcome it is supposed to predict out of sample. The acc(A_ret)−acc(A0) covariate guards against inert-memory cells but does nothing about this. Second, a checkable internal inconsistency: Prediction 1 requires per-cell TOST at a 4-point margin to pass in ≥8 of ~11 high-overlap cells, but Measurement §(b) states that at n=600 equivalence at margin 4 requires an observed gap ≤1.4, and §MDE gives n=300 → MDE ≈6, E2-broad n=140 → MDE ≈8, E2-narrow n=100 → MDE ≈9. Counting the A_fix cells actually planned, only about four run at n=600 (B_expel N=500, N=1000, the k=7 volume cell, B_rbank); the rest are n=300 subsamples (B-dup, A_rand, both cross-model families) or n=100–140 ALFWorld cells where TOST at a 4-point margin cannot pass even with a true zero difference. Prediction 1 as written is close to unachievable arithmetically, and Prediction 4's numeric claims for E2-narrow (R_fix < 2) and the ≥3-point narrow-vs-broad contrast are stated at a resolution below that cell's own declared MDE of 8–9.
what_would_fix_it: (a) Decontaminate the law. Report R_fix against an explicit analytic null: given the measured top-k sets and the frequency-selected fixed subset, compute the expected R_fix under a model in which the agent uses only the items common to both arms, and show that observed R_fix departs from that curve. Equivalently, restrict the headline regression to cells in a mid range (say O ∈ [0.2, 0.8]) at a single fixed k, and report the O ≈ 1 and B-dup cells as sanity endpoints rather than as data points that carry the fit. Without this, the paper's central number is a property of the definition of O, not of procedural memory. (b) Decouple k* selection from O by fixing k across the cells that enter the regression, and report the k*-selected version as a secondary. (c) Reconcile Prediction 1 with the MDE table: either drop per-cell TOST and make the inverse-variance random-effects meta-estimate the only equivalence claim (as Measurement §(b) already implies), or raise the margin and state honestly how many cells are powered. (d) Restate the E2 predictions as directional, since the design cannot resolve a 2-point R_fix at n=100. (e) Add the upper-bound retrieval arm named below, so a null on R_fix can be attributed to query conditioning rather than to a weak dense retriever — this is the single change that would most raise soundness, and it is cheap relative to the arms already budgeted.
missing_baseline: An upper-bound retrieval arm. The plan has A_rand as a lower bound but nothing above A_ret, so 'the retriever is decorative' cannot be separated from 'this dense/BM25 retriever extracts none of the available query-conditional signal' — which is precisely what the proposal's own mechanistic ally (2511.21730: embeddings treat procedures as bags of words, discarding temporal structure; LLM-generated abstractions transfer reliably) predicts is happening. Concretely: an oracle-relevance arm (select the k bank items whose source training instances are the gold-matched or human/LLM-labelled relevant ones for each test instance) and/or an LLM-reranker arm over the whole bank at the same k and matched tokens. If oracle retrieval also ties with A_fix, the claim is strong and general; if it beats A_fix by ≥4 points where dense retrieval does not, the paper's title is answered 'the retriever is bad, not decorative' and the deliverable diagnostic is measuring retriever weakness rather than a property of procedural memory. Secondary omission: a whole-bank-in-context arm without compilation at N=100 (the raw RAG-vs-long-context comparison the proposal invokes in Related Work §7 but never runs; A_comp is a frontier-model compilation, not stuffing).
preprint_collision: The check is unusually good by the standards of this genre — it quotes rather than paraphrases, explicitly withdraws five IDs an earlier draft relied on, reinstates Memp only because it reappeared in the current search, concedes that 2602.02751 outright scoops the bank-size saturation claim, and concedes 2511.21730 as a direction-level collision. I judge it honest and I do not find a preprint that already makes the specific overlap-predicts-premium claim. Three residual weaknesses, though, and they matter. First, the check is grounded entirely in one literature search's returns, with no OpenReview 2026 sweep and no independent verification pass; the author flags this as residual risk, which is the right disclosure but does not remove the exposure, given that a frozen-retrieved-subset ablation is exactly the kind of thing that lives in an appendix. Second, and more seriously, the check never searched the nearest neighbouring literature at all: retrieval-based versus fixed in-context demonstration selection, where the same swap has been run for years with frequently null results. The RAG-vs-long-context parallel is raised and answered, but the demonstration-selection parallel — which is the actual shape of A_fix — is absent from the search and from Related Work. An unsearched adjacent literature is a hole in the novelty argument, not a neutral. Third, the concessions the check does make add up to more than it concludes: with the direction attributed to 2511.21730/2602.02751/2606.23127 and the write-path abstraction to AWM/Auto-Dreamer, the entire remaining novelty rests on the overlap law and the MMR sign test — and the law is the component compromised by the definitional objection above, leaving the MMR discriminating test against 2606.29824 as the cleanest genuinely new thing in the proposal.
